# Appeal of Denied Prior Authorization — Lower Back Disc Surgery/Decompression (CPT 63030)

**RE:** Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-24
**Member:** Skyler Ellison
**Member ID:** W240749705
**Reference Number:** POC-1C51E72E1E-65750
**Plan:** PacificSource Health Plans (Commercial/ACA), State of Idaho
**Governing Policy:** Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Spine Surgery (https://guidelines.carelonmedicalbenefitsmanagement.com/spine-surgery-2025-11-15-updated-2026-01-01/)

Dear PacificSource Health Plans,

I am appealing the denial of coverage for my lower back disc surgery/decompression (CPT 63030), which my surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented as medically necessary. My request was denied for "incomplete documentation," but when I compare my medical records to your own published guideline, I believe the documentation on file addresses the criteria at issue. I am asking that you reconsider this denial.

## How my records match the plan's own criteria

**Conservative management before surgery.** Your guideline states:

> "Conservative management 1 must include a combination of strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and correct underlying dysfunction, including physical therapy AND at least ONE complementary conservative treatment strategy."

My records show I completed 24 visits of supervised physical therapy over 10 weeks (2026-04-24 to 2026-07-03), focused on core stabilization and lumbar flexibility, as documented in my physical therapy discharge note. This satisfies the physical therapy component.

**Complementary treatment strategies.** Your guideline lists acceptable complementary strategies, including:

> "Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics 2 Adjunctive medications such as nerve membrane stabilizers or muscle relaxants 2 Epidural corticosteroid injection(s) 2 Alternative therapies such as acupuncture, chiropractic manipulation, massage therapy, activity modification, and/or a trial period of rest (e.g., from the aggravating/contributing factors), where applicable"

My records show I used NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and I received an epidural corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-30, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief. This means I completed physical therapy *and* more than one complementary strategy, meeting the "at least ONE" requirement described above.

**Patient-specific, tailored program.** Your guideline calls for:

> "Participation in a patient-specific or tailored program Initial active instruction by MD/DO/PT with redemonstration of patient ability to perform exercises Compliance (documented or by clinician attestation on follow-up evaluation)"

My physical therapy was supervised and tailored to my condition (core stabilization and lumbar flexibility), and I completed all 24 scheduled visits, which reflects compliance with the program.

**Failure of conservative management.** Your guideline requires:

> "Failure of conservative management requires ALL the following:"
>
> "Patient has completed a full course of conservative management (as defined above) for the current episode of care Worsening of or no significant improvement in signs and/or symptoms upon clinical reevaluation More invasive forms of therapy are being considered Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

My records show I completed a full course of physical therapy, medication trial, and injection therapy for this episode, and that my pain has been unrelieved by rest for 12 months, with only 3 weeks of partial relief from the injection and inadequate relief from 8 months of NSAIDs. My surgeon is now recommending decompression surgery as a more invasive treatment. [If available, the specific reevaluation date and exam findings documenting lack of improvement after the full conservative course should be confirmed with my surgeon's office and included with this appeal.]

**Reevaluation.** Your guideline states:

> "2 In the absence of contraindications Clinical reevaluation – In most cases, reevaluation should include a physical examination."

My most recent exam findings include positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level, which reflect an in-person clinical reevaluation. [The specific date of this reevaluation exam should be confirmed with the medical records and included if not already part of the submitted packet.]

**Symptom severity and functional impact.** Your guideline states:

> "Reporting of symptom severity – Severity of pain and its associated impact on activities of daily living (ADLs) and instrumental ADLs (IADLs) are key factors in determining the need for intervention."
>
> "For purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated at least 3 out of 10 in intensity and associated with inability to perform at least two (2) ADLs and/or IADLs."

My records document that I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes and experience radicular pain radiating into my right calf, which reflects meaningful functional impairment. [A specific numeric pain rating (0–10 scale) and a second affected ADL/IADL are not included in the summary I have; if my surgeon's chart includes this, it should be added to support this criterion.]

**Imaging and clinical findings supporting the need for surgery.** My MRI of the lumbar spine, dated 2026-07-28, shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. My exam also shows a neurologic deficit corresponding to this imaged level. I believe this supports my surgeon's determination that continued conservative management alone is not enough at this point.

## What I am asking

I am asking PacificSource Health Plans to reconsider this denial in light of the records described above, which I believe address the plan's own documented criteria for conservative management, complementary treatment, and clinical reevaluation prior to lower back disc surgery. I am not asking for a guarantee of approval — only for a full review of the documentation against your own guideline.

## Deadline and how I am submitting this appeal

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-02-20**. I am submitting it as follows: [insert method used — e.g., electronic submission via InTouch "Ask a Question," email to NewAppeal@PacificSource.com, fax to 541-225-3628, or mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter]. I understand that electronic submission may be processed more quickly.

Please let me know if any additional information is needed from me or from Dr. Lindqvist's office to complete this review.

Sincerely,

_______________________________
Skyler Ellison
Member ID: W240749705
Date: [insert date of signature]
Phone: [insert phone number]
Email: [insert email address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
